back: Living traditions such as dances, songs, rituals, skills and knowledge passed on by a community.

front: Which dance was recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage?
back: Jerusarema/Mbende, of the Zezuru Shona of Murehwa and Mutoko.

front: Match the dances to their communities: Isitshikitsha, Muchongoyo, Mhande.
back: Isitshikitsha: Ndebele. Muchongoyo: Ndau and Shangani (south-east). Mhande: Karanga (Masvingo).
Using plays to raise awareness and discussion of social issues such as health, child marriage or the environment.

front: Which bodies oversee the arts and sport in Zimbabwe?
back: The National Arts Council of Zimbabwe (arts) and the Sports and Recreation Commission (sport).

front: Give six reasons why sport, arts and culture are important.
back: Entertainment, socialisation, identity, unity, health, employment (also tourism, national pride, education).

front: How do traditional dances support tourism?
back: Visitors pay to see living culture and spend money on food, crafts and lodging, creating income and jobs.

front: Name three challenges facing artists and athletes.
back: Low and irregular pay, piracy, lack of facilities and equipment, cost of travel, migration of talent.
